newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania calls tender for tourism companies.
newsitem.headline: Romania calls tender for tourism companies.

text.p: Romania will call a tender to sell five hotels and two travel agencies this month, in the first major bid to restructure and relaunch the sector, the Tourism Minister said on Wednesday.

Akos Birtalan told a news conference the offer in the tender scheduled for May 23 included the purchase of a 40 percent stake in five hotels located on the Black Sea coast and in the mountain areas, as well as two travel agencies.
The remaining 60 percent of shares in those companies are currently held by thousands of shareholders as a result of Romania's mass selloff scheme completed last year.

The tender is part of a major programme launched by the tourism ministry last month to put into private hands 53 companies in the sector, including hotels on the Black Sea coast and the mountain areas as well as in towns with tourist potential.

"Shares in all 53 companies will be sold rapidly, at their market value. There is no minimum price, the best offer will prevail," Birtalan said, adding that tenders for the remaining companies would be called on a weekly basis.
Privatisation in Romania's tourism sector was brought to a halt during the tenure of the former leftist cabinet, ousted in last November's elections.
Data shows tourism accounts for only two percent of Romania's gross domestic product while real privatisation in the sector amounts to a mere 4.2 percent.
The new centrist government pledged to step up reforms in the tourism sector in a bid to bring visitors and major Western tour operators back to the Balkan country.
